instruction: Use Abaqus to perform a simply supported beam analysis under a uniformly distributed load. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a 10 mm x 10 mm rectangle in the Y-Z plane and extrude along the global X-axis to a length of 200 mm. This produces a beam with cross-section 10 mm x 10 mm and span 200 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Solid Homogeneous section using Steel and assign it to the entire beam. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the beam. Analysis Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-Load. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Create a reference point RP-1 at the geometric center of the left end face (X = 0, Y = 5 mm, Z = 5 mm) and couple it kinematically to that end face. Create a reference point RP-2 at the geometric center of the right end face (X = 200 mm, Y = 5 mm, Z = 5 mm) and couple it kinematically to that end face. At RP-1, constrain U1 = U2 = U3 = 0 and UR2 = UR3 = 0 to model a pinned support that allows rotation about the beam axis (UR1). At RP-2, constrain U2 = U3 = 0 and UR2 = UR3 = 0 to model a roller support that allows axial motion (U1) and rotation about the beam axis (UR1). Apply a pressure of 0.05 MPa downward on the beam top surface (Y = 10 mm face). This loading is equivalent to a uniformly distributed load q = 0.5 N/mm. Discretization: Mesh the beam with a global seed size of 5 mm. Assign the element type C3D8R and generate the mesh. Job Execution: Create a job named Job-UDL, submit it for analysis, and wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Deliverables: Save the model database as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-UDL.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-UDL.odb. Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.
